title: Fashion brand ATACAC discusses their experience using CLO
transcript: There's the real world and there's the virtual world, and increasingly in the future, you will constantly move between the two, and we want to dress people in both worlds. When we decided to start Atta Kack three years ago, at the same time we came across Clow and realized that what I had been doing for ten years prior—physically draping fabrics on live models—is now largely possible to do digitally. When we start the design process and do it digitally, we end up with a digital product, which then makes it possible to do it digitally. When we start the design process and do it digitally, we end up with a digital product, which then makes it possible to both present it immediately, instantly. So for us, the same day we have designed something, we can actually start to sell it in an online store or post the design process on social media to show what we do and see if we get any feedback on it. Today, Atta Kack works as both a fashion brand and a fashion consultancy studio where we have the opportunity to try different potential solutions that 3D technology gives us, both in a small-scale brand and with larger enterprises. That's part of our vision: to inspire other brands to digitize themselves; it's a very creative way of working. Our aim for Atta Kack is to be the world’s most relevant fashion brand, and working with 3D visualization is a central part of that. Yeah, maybe in the future we will sell more virtual garments than physical ones. It’s a very fun time with so many possibilities. It feels endless now. We have lists of ideas we just want to do. We use the 3D tools to create our own designs. And the 3D tools include everything from styling to grading to design development to animation to fittings. It really affects all stages of what we’re doing.

chunks.title: Fashion brand ATACAC discusses their experience using CLO
chunks.content: ## Digital and Physical Fashion Integration at ATACAC This section explains ATACAC's vision of blending the real and virtual worlds through digital fashion design, highlighting the use of CLO software to digitize traditional garment creation processes. ATACAC was founded three years ago with the goal of dressing people in both real and virtual environments. Around the same time, they discovered CLO, a 3D garment visualization tool that transformed their decade-long experience of physically draping fabrics on live models into a fully digital process. By starting the design process digitally, they produce a digital product that can be immediately presented, shared, and sold. This digital-first workflow allows ATACAC to design and showcase new garments on the same day, posting designs on social media or launching them directly in their online store to gather instant feedback. This rapid iteration and presentation model exemplifies the efficiency gained by integrating CLO’s technology into fashion design. ## ATACAC’s Dual Role: Fashion Brand and Consultancy This section covers ATACAC’s combined business model as a fashion brand and consultancy, focusing on their exploration of 3D technology applications at different scales and their broader vision to inspire digital transformation in fashion. Beyond operating as a fashion brand, ATACAC also functions as a fashion consultancy studio. This dual role enables them to experiment with various 3D technology solutions, both for their own small-scale brand and in collaboration with larger enterprises. This experimentation fuels their vision to encourage other brands to digitize their design and production workflows, emphasizing creativity and innovation in the digital realm. Their ambition is to become the world’s most relevant fashion brand by leveraging 3D visualization as a core part of their identity. They acknowledge a future where virtual garments may outsell physical ones, reflecting the growing importance and potential of digital fashion. ## Comprehensive Use of 3D Tools in Fashion Design This section details how ATACAC utilizes 3D software tools throughout the entire design and production process, including styling, grading, animation, and fittings. ATACAC employs a wide range of 3D tools integrated within CLO’s platform to support every stage of their design workflow. These tools cover: - Styling: Creating and refining the visual appearance of garments. - Grading: Adjusting patterns to different sizes digitally. - Design Development: Iterating on garment designs in a virtual environment. - Animation: Simulating garment movement and fit on digital models. - Fittings: Virtually fitting garments on avatars to evaluate drape and fit before physical production. This comprehensive use of 3D technology enhances efficiency, reduces reliance on physical samples, and opens new creative possibilities. ATACAC views this digital approach as a transformative advancement in fashion design.
